validated_results.title: Macronutrient intake and risk of urothelial cell carcinoma in the European prospective investigation into cancer and nutrition.
validated_results.reason: Prospective EPIC cohort reporting incident urothelial cell carcinoma risk in relation to dietary animal protein intake, with a target-specific hazard estimate.

extraction.comparison_type: Per 3% increase in energy intake from animal protein
extraction.population: Men and women in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition
extraction.smoking_status: Adjusted for smoking status and duration

sample_size.excerpt: We examined macronutrient intake in relation to risk of urothelial cell carcinoma among 469,339 men and women in the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition.

cases.excerpt: After an average of 11.3 years of follow-up, 1,416 new cases of urothelial cell carcinoma were identified.

effect_size.excerpt: After allowing for measurement error, a 3% increase in the consumption of energy intake from animal protein was associated with a 15% higher risk (95% confidence interval [CI]: 3-30%; p(trend) = 0.01) and a 2% increase in energy from plant protein intake was associated with a 23% lower risk (95% CI: 36-7%, p(trend) = 0.006). Dietary intake of fat, carbohydrate, fibre or calcium was not associated with risk.

comparison.excerpt: a 3% increase in the consumption of energy intake from animal protein

design.excerpt: Associations were examined using Cox regression, stratified by sex, age at recruitment and centre

timing.excerpt: After an average of 11.3 years of follow-up

continent.excerpt: European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition

exposure_measurement.excerpt: We examined macronutrient intake in relation to risk of urothelial cell carcinoma

smoking_status.excerpt: further adjusted for smoking status and duration

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
extraction.ethnicity_basis: NA: no field-specific ethnicity evidence was available
